findings.message: put_blob always decodes the bytes with errors="replace" and stores the re-encoded text. Any input that is not valid UTF-8 is changed for good: invalid bytes become U+FFFD, and get_blob(ref) returns those changed bytes instead of the data that was put. That breaks the round-trip AC5 asks for, and the stdout_times blob is a list of nanosecond offsets that may well be binary. Different invalid inputs can also collapse to one ref.
findings.paved_road: Decode with errors="strict". If decoding succeeds, run the redactor on the text and hash the re-encoded result. If it raises UnicodeDecodeError, hash and store the raw bytes unchanged. Add a test that puts non-UTF-8 bytes and checks get_blob returns them exactly.

findings.message: prune collects references only from end.json files. When it decides whether a newer record still uses a blob, it ignores start.json (prompt.blob), normalized/*.json (args_blob, output_blob, text_blob) and calls that have a start.json but no end.json yet. Blobs are content-addressed and deduplicated, so a blob listed in the oldest end.json can be the same blob as a newer record's prompt, a normalized view's blob, or the output of a call still running. prune deletes it and leaves that newer record pointing at a missing blob. The ticket says a blob referenced by a newer record stays.
findings.paved_road: Build the set of protected refs from every file under calls/<key>/ (start.json, end.json and normalized/*). Only delete refs that appear in the oldest end.json and in no newer record and no in-flight call.

findings.message: For each record, prune builds the union of the refs of every newer record again, so its cost is O(n^2) in the number of records. The design runs prune after every end.json write, and a store near the 20 GB bound can hold tens of thousands of calls, so each prune would do billions of set operations.
findings.paved_road: Count how many records reference each blob (or build the newer-ref sets once, walking from newest to oldest). Then walk the records from oldest to newest, decrementing counts, and delete a blob when its count reaches zero.

findings.message: write_record("event") writes one Event as the whole calls/<key>/normalized/<normalizer>.json file. FileSystem.publish refuses an existing destination, so writing a second event for the same call and normalizer raises FileExistsError. The design (Record layout, section 3) says that file holds the normalizer's list of events, so this path cannot store a real normalized view.
findings.paved_road: Have the event record path take and validate a list of Event models and write it as one file, or drop the event case from write_record and read_record until the normalizer ticket defines that file's format.
